summary: The root LWY primarily signifies bending, twisting, or turning something. It can also denote evading, delaying, or distorting.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: لَوَى عَلَيْهِ He waited for him. (Msb.) مَرَّ لَا يَلْوِى عَلَى أَحَدٍ He went along, not pausing nor waiting for any one. (Msb.) See the Kur-án, iii. 147. لَوَاهُ بِدَيْنِهِ i. q. مَطَلَهُ. (S, Msb, K.) لَوَى He twisted a thing; turned or wreathed it round or about: contorted it: wound it: curled it: curved it: or bent it. (K, &c.) And He, or it, turned him from his course; made him to deviate, or swerve. لَوَى عَلَيْهِ He went round it, or round about it. (Bd, in liii.
أَلْوَى بِالكَلَامِ He distorted, wrested, or wrung, the language. (M, K.) [Hence, perhaps, فُلَانٌ يُلْوِى بِخَصْمِهِ, if the verb be correctly thus: see عُقْمِىَ, last sentence.]

تَلَوَّى ألوى لوى لوي تلو تلوى تلوي It twisted, or coiled, itself: (KL:) it became twisted, or coiled: one says, تَلَوَّتِ الحَيَّةُ. (MA.) تَلَوَّى مِنْ وَجَعِ الضَّرْبِ [ He writhed by reason of the pain of beating ]. (M, A, K, art. ضور.)
يَتَلاَوَيَانِ said of two serpents [ They twist together ]: see عَقاَمٌ, last sentence.

اِلْتَوَى, neuter verb, It twisted: wound: bent. (K, &c.) اِلْتَوَى عَلَيْهِ It (an affair) became difficult; or difficult and intricate. (TA.) الْتَوَتْ عَلَىَّ حَاجَتِى My want became difficult of attainment. (TA.) التوى عَلَيْهِ also He acted, or behaved, perversely towards him.

لِوَآءٌ A banner, or standard, syn. عَلَمٌ, (M, Mgh, K,) of a commander, (T,) or of an army, less than the رَايَة, being a strip of cloth, twisted, or wound, and tied to a spear-shaft. (Mgh.) See رِفَادَةٌ. Respecting the لِوَآء of the Kaabeh, see سَدَنَ and فَادَةٌ.
اللَّوَا occurs in poetry for اللَّوَاتِى. (TA in art. شرف.)
أَلْوَى Very contentious. (K.) See an ex. voce مُسْتَمَرّ.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
